problem_statement: A retained native result can be silently detached from changed source bytes, a missing JSON row, another test function or an incomplete capture inventory. Treating a structurally valid subset as complete would conceal unreviewed native questions. The proof consumer needs to distinguish exact retained evidence from an output assertion or coverage claim borrowed from another owner.
question: Does the proof gate reject changed evidence, missing row selectors, escaping paths, adjacent-function comment donation, unindexed pages/test annotations, suppressed JSON candidate flags and pending capture coverage while keeping structural audit distinct from complete certification?
conclusion: The gate checks complete file digests and selected rows, repository-contained paths, exact question/document/provider bindings and the current corpus census. Every proof page and explicitly marked Rust question requires an indexed record. A retained JSON capture cannot escape review by clearing its candidate flag. Pending capture review and unlinked tests fail complete certification. Structural audit neither executes a native probe nor certifies completed coverage.
scope: Python proof-consumer implementation contract. The fixed synthetic controls exercise validator rejection paths; they do not constitute C Tcl, Jim or BIG-IP language observations.
